$comment: A machine-readable claim about what the product implements. CI runs
scripts/check-feature-matrix.py, which verifies that every capability marked 'complete' names a
Tauri command that exists and test files that exist. A capability is only 'complete' when the
product can actually reach it and a test actually covers it.
Status values are deliberately three-way. 'partial' exists so a half-finished capability is
visible rather than being rounded up to 'complete' or hidden entirely.

capabilities.summary: Partially observable grid planning with a replayable seed.
A capability-gated task where the process capability is real and executed; filesystem, network, and environment capabilities are authorized and refused at execution time, not executed.
One authoritative agent description that the UI renders and the runner builds through, with per-agent game compatibility.
Benchmarks declare their capability-execution mode and replay support in the registry rather than in UI copy.
A read-only projection of the real orchestrator: phase, plan decisions, monitoring signals, and the experiment's own event timeline.
Turns a plan into episodes, results, a timeline, and a terminal state. Holds no broker, no policy, and no containment handle, so it is structurally incapable of authorizing.
A real match through the engine's play_match, with per-ply board history from the engine's own telemetry. Two policies are registered, one a perfect ceiling.
Schema exists in GameBoard and GameKind; no engine implementation, so it is not offered rather than offered and left to fail.
Schema exists; no engine implementation.
Schema exists; no engine implementation.
No human-turn path. A human player would be a second execution path with its own state transitions, in a panel whose value is that the environment is the only thing that moves the board.
Runs the registry's six security probes through the real broker and sandbox path and reports which layer acted. A caught attempt is a successful test, not a vulnerability.
Reconstructs recorded frames deterministically. Holds no provider, broker, launcher, or engine, so it cannot call a model or execute anything.

Stored experiments can be compared, ranked by success fraction, mean reward, mean turns, and mean invalid actions. A run with no completed episode has no score, no rank, and a stated reason -- it is never shown as 0%. Equal measurements share a rank, and every success fraction carries its Wilson interval, so a one-episode run is visibly weaker evidence rather than a better agent. Two runs are refused outright when their benchmark or root seed differ, because they are not measuring the same thing. Differing agent, adapter, or strategy is a confound rather than a blocker -- refusing that would make the feature useless -- so the comparison is produced and every unheld identity is declared above the rankings. The panel renders the backend decision and computes nothing itself.
No settings panel. Provider configuration is currently per-run.
The OpenAI-compatible chat-completions path, verified working against a local Ollama. Also reaches vLLM, LM Studio, and llama.cpp where they expose /v1.
The Anthropic Messages API: version header, top-level system prompt, and multi-block content joined so a truncated-looking reply is not misreported as unparseable.
The Gemini generateContent API, with the model name constrained so it cannot redirect a request out of the intended endpoint.
Deliberately absent. The verified OpenAI-compatible path already reaches Ollama; a native /api/chat adapter would add a second thing to test without adding a capability.
Deliberately absent. OpenCode is a coding agent, not a model endpoint; there is no API to point at.
The only capability authorization authority. Review, grant, and refuse filesystem, network, process, and environment requests under an explicit policy.

Windows AppContainer containment: a derived per-run SID, a designated writable directory, protected paths, job limits, and a fail-closed refusal when the identity cannot be placed in force. Not complete OS isolation.

One authoritative product execution path. The Runner draws episode seeds from the benchmark own declared evaluation pool, disjoint from its development seeds, and reports a Wilson interval via the engine function rather than its own. A failed episode is recorded and skipped, each episode gets a fresh RunContext, and mean_success_fraction() is None when nothing completed. The separate Harness remains for offline benchmark discrimination measurement, where fail-fast is correct.

Seven destinations in a persistent sidebar, hash-routed and deep-linkable, each showing one panel: command center, agents, benchmarks, providers, arena, security, replay. The active destination is marked by colour, a left bar, and aria-current, so it is not signalled by colour alone. The nav is a real button list in a labelled landmark: Tab leaves it, arrow keys and Home/End move within it, and focus follows the selection. A skip link bypasses the nav on every page. Every nav item opens a panel that exists; there are no disabled or coming-soon entries. No routing dependency is used.

Results and telemetry persist to SQLite under an immutability trigger. Experiment lifecycle is a separate five-state record: planned, running, completed, failed, interrupted. The running state is written before the first episode, so a crash leaves evidence; on the next start every row still saying running is transitioned to interrupted, because that is provably false. A crashed run is never reported completed. Partial episodes are preserved but are not a complete measurement. There is no resume.

Every type that crosses a process or storage boundary has its field names and enum spellings pinned against hand-written JSON literals, in both directions. A round-trip test alone would pass when both ends drift together, which is the one case that does not matter; the defect that motivated this shipped as SecurityProbe where the wire format is security_probe, with every test green. Three properties are asserted: field names, that every boundary enum is snake_case, and that an absent optional stays absent -- a missing score that decodes to 0.0 is a measurement the product did not make. Unknown variants are rejected rather than defaulted, so a corrupted row cannot become a plausible-looking state. Two naming rules are in deliberate use and are documented where they are asserted: structs the frontend reads are camelCase, everything else is snake_case, and CapabilityPermission keeps its dotted names because stored policy documents have always used them. CI runs this as a named target, so deleting the file fails the step instead of quietly matching zero tests -- the previous filter passed while running none.
